div.head: Leis Wl 47.1
div.ab: E s’il ne volt, sil [v]e[ncu]ist l’um vif u mort, si prenge l’um quanque il ad, e si rende l’um al chalangeur sun chatel, e li sire ait la meité del remenant e le hundred la meité.
Quodsi nec sic copiam sui fecerit, [uin]dicetur siue uiuus siue mortuus, capiaturque quicquid habet, et, redditis calumpniatoribus catallis, residuum diuidant inter se ex equo dominus et hundredus.
E s'il ne volt, sil [v]e[ncu]ist l'um vif u mort, si prenge l'um quanque il ad, e si rende l'um al chalangeur sun chatel, e li sire ait la meité del remenant e le hundred la meité.

47, 1. Wenn er jedoch sich weigert, so überwinde man ihn, lebend oder todt, und nehme man alles, was er hat, fort, und erstatte man dem Kläger dessen [eingeklagtes] Werthstück, und vom Übrigen erhalte der Herr [des Verbrechers] die Hälfte und die Hundertschaft die Hälfte.

47, 1. If, however, he refuses, then one shall overcome him, living or dead, and one shall take away everything he has, and one shall restore to the plaintiff his [sued-for] article of value, and of the remainder the lord [of the criminal] shall receive half and the hundred half.

And if he refuses, he shall be seized, alive or dead, and all that he has shall be taken, and the value of his goods shall be paid to the claimant, and the lord [of the thief] shall take half of what remains and the hundred half.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 274–275 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 518, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)
